title: Cut an image into a circle

seo.metaTitle: Cut a PNG Into a Circle - Free Mask, No Upload Needed
seo.metaDescription: Trim an image to a circle with a movable center: pick the diameter as a share of the shorter side. Free and unlimited, processed right in your browser.
seo.longDescription: Cut an image into a circle keeps the pixels inside a circle and makes everything outside it transparent. The Shape size slider sets the diameter as a share of the shorter side of the picture, so 100 on a 1200 by 800 image produces a circle 800 pixels wide, and Offset moves that circle into the free space around it. The picture is not resized and its colors are not touched; only the corners lose their opacity. The cut is a hard edge with no anti-aliasing, and the result is written in your browser without an upload.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Shape size from 20 to 100 — the diameter as a share of the shorter side.
The canvas keeps its size; everything outside the circle becomes transparent.
Hard edge, no anti-aliasing — run feather edges for a soft rim.
Save as PNG or WebP to keep the transparent corners.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Set Shape size from 20 to 100; the diameter is a share of the shorter side.
Move the circle with Offset if it should not sit in the middle.
Turn on Show mask to see the shape alone, then download the result.

faq.a: No. The canvas keeps its size and everything outside the circle becomes transparent instead of being deleted. Use trim empty space afterwards if you want the frame tightened around the circle.

faq.q: Why is my circle smaller than I expected on a wide photo?
faq.a: Shape size is measured against the shorter side, so on a landscape photo 100 means a circle as tall as the picture and centered, with empty margins at the sides.

faq.q: Can I keep the transparency when I save?
faq.a: Yes, as long as you pick PNG or WebP in the Download button. JPG and BMP have no alpha channel, so the corners come out as a flat background color there.
